findings.title: End-slot matching can still write past the starting-node table when swapping the primary tree
findings.evidence: The new start/link capacity and loop guards do not guard swap_waypoint_nodes final resolved indices. match_end_slots can select node_index 0 for a swap when host-supplied positions place another same-depth leaf at the requested slot. On different trees, swap_waypoint_nodes ascends to their roots, then searches waypoint_starting_nodes from index 1. A selected primary root at index 0 is not found. With 24 valid starts, the search returns 24; the existing ASSERT is the only check before writing waypoint_starting_nodes[24]. The new outer 4096-pass limit is reached after this unsafe write and cannot protect it.
findings.source_only_shape: A bounded 24-tree forest, each with a same-depth leaf, fits the new start/link limits and makes progress normally. A primary branch identifies the first tree. Host-controlled leaf positions can cause end-slot matching to exchange the index-0 leaf with another tree. This is a source-backed counterexample, not a native execution or retail-data claim.
findings.required_change: Validate each resolved root-swap index against the actual starting-node count and array capacity before ASSERT and before either write, with a named host-route refusal. Preserve valid original matching order and policy; do not silently skip or redirect index 0. Keep any corresponding common-parent child-index writes subject to a proven lookup-success condition or a named prewrite check. Add only a bounded corrected-source guard control; never run this shape on the known-unsafe old or 50e native.
findings.impact: Residual of the same untrusted topology/workspace boundary; prevents finite production-route slice closure.
